name: Moses
role: Prophet, lawgiver, and leader of the exodus
whenBasis: 1 Kings 6:1 puts the exodus 480 years before Solomon's fourth year, ≈1446 BC. Many historians put it under Ramesses II, ≈1270s–1250s BC, taking Exodus 1:11's store city Rameses as his. The text gives no date in any calendar we can fix.
summary: A Levite hidden in the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter, Moses fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian and met the LORD in the burning bush. He led Israel out of Egypt, received the Law at Sinai, led the people forty years in the wilderness, and died on Mount Nebo in sight of the land.
body: Born when Pharaoh has ordered Hebrew boys drowned, he is set afloat in a basket, found by Pharaoh's daughter and nursed by his own mother. She names him Moses, “I drew him out of the water.” Grown, he kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew and flees to Midian, where he marries Zipporah and keeps Jethro's flocks.

At Horeb the LORD speaks from a bush that burns and is not consumed, gives his name, “I AM WHO I AM,” and sends him back. With Aaron he confronts Pharaoh through ten plagues; after the Passover Israel leaves, and the sea is divided.

At Sinai he receives the Law and the tablets, smashes them over the golden calf, and intercedes for the people. For striking the rock at Meribah instead of speaking to it he is barred from entering the land. He sees it from Nebo and dies in Moab; “no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.”

moments.text: Drawn from the water and named
Called up the mountain for the tablets
Sees the land from Nebo, and dies

later.text: Tradition holds that Moses wrote the Torah; the Talmud gives the last eight verses, on his death, to Joshua. Most critical scholars see the five books as compiled from several sources long after him.

sources.note: 480 years from the exodus to Solomon's fourth year
